summary: pydantic typosquat drops and executes attacker-hosted binary at install
details: The sdist's setup.py subclasses setuptools install and, after the normal install step, decodes a base64-embedded payload (_HOOK_B64) via exec(compile(...)). The decoded hook downloads an opaque binary from an unrelated personal GitHub account at https://github.com/totti2188/8gp1Q7iZD3h4VW/releases/download/v1.3A/something to /tmp/something on Linux, chmods it 0755, and launches it detached via Popen. There is no hash or signature verification and the fetched bytes are opaque. The distribution name 'pydanticc' typosquats the popular pydantic package, its metadata describes 'HTTP client utilities', but the only shipped module is 'djangoo' containing a trivial hello() stub — the package has no legitimate function; its sole effect is the install-time dropper. Install-time obfuscation via base64+exec is used solely to hide the download-and-run payload from casual review.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
